A useful second plan.
Our class planned a nature day near a lake. On Friday, the teacher showed us two plans. "If the weather is fine, we will walk along the field and take photographs," she said. "If it rains heavily, we will stay at school and use the hall." I wanted the outdoor plan because I enjoyed watching wildlife. Jo preferred the indoor table, where we could compare leaves. On Saturday morning, dark clouds covered the sky and rain began before breakfast. At school, the teacher chose the indoor plan. At first, I thought the day would be boring. Then our group opened a box of leaves from the school garden. Some were the same shape, but their colors and edges were different. We used a guidebook to work out which tree each leaf came from. Sam took close photographs, and I wrote short labels. When we compared our work, every group noticed something the others missed. Near the end, the rain stopped. There was no time for the lake, so we finished our display instead. I was pleased with what we made. The teacher said we could plan another visit next week. If the weather is fine, we will go outside then. A good second plan helped us enjoy today.
